reason: Pure-Python library whose README Usage examples (signed-data verification, promotional offer signatures) run offline on CPU using bundled test keys/certs with no Apple account needed.
demo: README Usage: 'Verification Usage' (SignedDataVerifier), 'Receipt Usage' (ReceiptUtility) and 'Promotional Offer Signature Creation'
goal: Install the library from the repo (pip install of the clone, Python 3.8+) so that `appstoreserverlibrary` imports. Then, using the bundled test files tests/resources/certs/testCA.der, tests/resources/certs/testSigningKey.p8, tests/resources/mock_signed_data/{testNotification,transactionInfo} and tests/resources/xcode/xcode-app-receipt-with-transaction, make SignedDataVerifier (online checks disabled, SANDBOX, bundle id com.example, app id 1234) decode the notification and the transaction, make PromotionalOfferSignatureCreator produce a signature, and make ReceiptUtility extract the transaction id from the Xcode app receipt. No Apple credentials or network API calls are needed.
check: A Python script imports the installed library, creates a promotional offer signature that verifies against the test key, decodes the bundled notification (type TEST) and transaction, checks that a wrong bundle id is rejected, and extracts the transaction id from the bundled Xcode receipt.

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: The verifier is built with default strict X509 checks, which the bundled test certs can't pass (they have no authority key identifiers). The repo's own tests disable strict checks for this reason, so a correct install always fails

Coverage is thin: of the README's offline usage sections only signature creation and notification decoding are tested. v2 adds transaction decoding, a negative check (a wrong bundle id must be rejected, so an accept-everything verifier fails) and README 'Receipt Usage' (ReceiptUtility on the bundled Xcode receipt -> '0'). The goal and check are updated to name these
evidence: tests/util.py:36-39 - verifier._chain_verifier.enable_strict_checks = False # We don't have authority identifiers on test certs
tests/test_payload_verification.py:34-38,74-85 - notification TEST, transaction SANDBOX, wrong bundle -> INVALID_APP_IDENTIFIER
data/runs/apple-app-store-server-l-eeba5/result.json audit - repo test passes with strict checks off; signature part already passed
